title: Bounded-below complexes admit bounded-below K-injective resolutions
statement: Let $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be a ringed site with small underlying category, and let $\mathcal G^\bullet$ be a bounded-below cochain complex of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then there is a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ to a bounded-below cochain complex whose terms are injective $\mathcal O_U$-modules, and $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

source.place: Tag 07A5 (Section 21.19, sites-cohomology-section-unbounded), using Tag 079P (Theorem 19.12.6, injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck); the bounded-below form is obtained by the standard truncation of the construction at the lower bound

proof.text: The category $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules on the small ringed site $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (its first clause), hence it is abelian and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives].

Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] to the bounded-below complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ in this abelian category. It yields a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\mathcal I^\bullet$ bounded below and every $\mathcal I^n$ injective.
A bounded-below complex whose terms are injective is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so the resulting $\mathcal I^\bullet$ has the required K-injective property.
